current.text: Tre Jones is expected to be the Bulls' sixth man and backup point guard. Josh Giddey and Norman Powell start ahead of him. Isaac Okoro and Buddy Hield come off the bench behind him.
Experts expect a smaller role than last season, when he started only because of injuries and departures. They see about 23 to 25 minutes a game off the bench at most.
His efficiency gains from last season, mainly his high field goal percentage, are expected to come back down.
The market drafts him too high. Experts put him in the last-pick range, a tier 9 point guard, and call an ADP of about 110 too high.
His upside depends on an injury to Giddey or an injury to or trade of Powell. If one of them goes down, he becomes a great waiver pickup.
The Bulls front office signs veterans on short deals, Powell among them, and hopes to trade them. That could open a starting role for Jones.
The Bulls are projected to be one of the worse teams in the league.
With a March 28 end, the Bulls play 3, 3 and 4 games in fantasy playoff weeks 19 to 21 (10 games). They have 15 back-to-backs, one below the maximum.

durable.text: He is a really good facilitator.
He is a poor three-point shooter and gets few rebounds.
His category value comes from FG%, which is high for a guard, plus assists and few turnovers. He gives little in threes and blocks.
